description: Health of the in-process Kubernetes Gateway API / Ingress controller: leadership, sync freshness, reconcile results and timing, watch load, the generated routing model, and traffic per Kubernetes route.

panels.title: Controllers
panels.description: Trickster processes in the selection that are running the in-process Kubernetes controller (they have completed at least one reconcile pass). The shipped controller Deployment runs 2. 0 means no selected process has a kubernetes section enabled.

targets.expr: count(group(trickster_kgw_reconciles_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}) by (job, instance))

panels.title: Leaders
panels.description: Controller replicas holding the leader-election Lease, per scrape job; the leader writes status and Events, every replica serves traffic. Expect 1. 0 is normal when leader_election.enabled is false (every replica writes status but none reports leadership) or read_only is true; with election on, 0 for longer than lease_duration (15s by default) means no replica is writing status. Above 1 is two scrapes straddling a handover, or two controller deployments in one job.

targets.expr: sum by (job) (trickster_kgw_leader{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"} and on (job, instance) group(trickster_kgw_reconciles_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}) by (job, instance))

panels.title: Since last sync
panels.description: Time since the most stale controller replica last finished a reconcile pass whose compile and publish succeeded, i.e. since its data plane last matched the cluster. Informer resyncs run a pass every resync_interval (10m by default) even when nothing changes, so much more than that means passes are failing. 'never synced' is a replica that has reconciled but never succeeded; n/a means no selected process runs the controller.

targets.expr: max((time() - (trickster_kgw_last_successful_sync_time_seconds{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"} > 0)) or on (job, instance) (group(trickster_kgw_reconciles_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}) by (job, instance) * 0 + 1e12)) or vector(-1)

panels.title: Failed passes
panels.description: Share of reconcile passes over the visible range whose compile or publish failed; such a pass leaves the last good configuration serving. Certificate and status problems do not fail a pass (see Cert rejections and Status failures). Healthy is 0.

targets.expr: (sum(increase(trickster_kgw_reconciles_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", result="error"}[$__range])) or vector(0)) / clamp_min(sum(increase(trickster_kgw_reconciles_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__range])), 1e-9)

panels.title: Cert rejections
panels.description: Reconcile passes over the visible range in which a listener's certificate store refused one or more certificates from Kubernetes TLS Secrets (missing, unparsable or mismatched material). The rest of the pass still applies and the certificate already serving stays in place; the object gets a CertificateRejected Event. Counted on every replica.

targets.expr: sum(increase(trickster_kgw_reconcile_errors_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", stage="certificates"}[$__range])) or vector(0)

panels.title: Status failures
panels.description: Kubernetes objects whose status update the API server refused over the visible range (after conflict retries), counted per object on the replica that writes status. Most often missing RBAC status verbs. Failed writes are retried on the next pass, so a persistent problem keeps counting.

targets.expr: sum(increase(trickster_kgw_status_write_failures_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__range])) or vector(0)

panels.title: Routed objects
panels.description: Kubernetes route objects (HTTPRoute, GRPCRoute, TCPRoute, TLSRoute, UDPRoute and Ingress) the last compiled pass serves, across the selected replicas. Objects the controller refused are not counted. The Backend filter applies.

targets.expr: count(group by (kind, namespace, route) (group by (backend_name, kind, namespace, route) (label_replace(trickster_kgw_route_info{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}, "namespace", "$1", "exported_namespace", "(.+)"))))

panels.title: Divergence
panels.description: Largest difference between replicas in any routing-model object count (listeners, routes, backends, certificates, policies). Every replica translates the same cluster, so this should be 0; it is briefly nonzero while a change rolls through the replicas, and a lasting value means one replica is stuck on an older model.

targets.expr: max(max by (kind) (trickster_kgw_generated_objects{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}) - min by (kind) (trickster_kgw_generated_objects{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}))

panels.title: Reconcile passes by result
panels.description: Reconcile passes per minute on each replica. applied = a changed configuration was published and the data plane reloaded; unchanged = the cluster changed nothing Trickster serves (also informer resyncs every resync_interval, and passes superseded by a newer configuration); error = compile or publish failed and the last good configuration kept serving. Watch events are debounced, so a burst of changes yields one pass.

targets.expr: sum by (instance, result) (rate(trickster_kgw_reconciles_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])) * 60

panels.title: Mean duration by phase
panels.description: Average time per reconcile pass across the selected replicas (translate, compile, publish, certificate push; status writes run on a separate worker and are excluded), of translating watched objects into the routing model, and of publishing a changed configuration to the data plane (only on passes that change it, including failed publishes). Means are used because the histograms' smallest bucket is 50 ms, so quantiles below it are interpolation. Lines join sparse passes.

targets.expr: sum(rate(trickster_kgw_reconcile_duration_seconds_sum{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])) / (sum(rate(trickster_kgw_reconcile_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)

sum(rate(trickster_kgw_translate_duration_seconds_sum{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])) / (sum(rate(trickster_kgw_translate_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)

sum(rate(trickster_kgw_apply_duration_seconds_sum{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])) / (sum(rate(trickster_kgw_apply_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)

panels.title: Reconcile duration distribution
panels.description: Reconcile passes per duration bucket over time, across the selected replicas. Buckets are 50 ms, 100 ms, 500 ms, 1 s, 5 s, 10 s and 20 s, so most passes land in the first row; passes climbing into the 1 s+ rows point at a very large cluster or a slow data-plane reload.

targets.expr: sum by (le) (increase(trickster_kgw_reconcile_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval]) and on (job, instance) group(trickster_kgw_reconciles_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}) by (job, instance))

panels.title: Reconcile errors by stage
panels.description: Errors per minute on each replica, by stage. compile and apply failed the pass (the last good configuration keeps serving) and usually happen on every replica at once. certificates = a listener refused a certificate, the pass otherwise applied. status = a status-writer job in which at least one object's write failed, counted once per job on the replica writing status, so it does not match Status write failures by kind one for one.

targets.expr: sum by (instance, stage) (rate(trickster_kgw_reconcile_errors_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])) * 60

panels.title: Leader by replica
panels.description: Which controller replica held the leader-election Lease over time. Every replica keeps serving; only the leader writes status and Events. A replica that loses the Lease stops writing at once. All replicas standby throughout means leader election is disabled (every replica writes) or the controller is read_only.

targets.expr: max by (instance) (trickster_kgw_leader{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"} and on (job, instance) group(trickster_kgw_reconciles_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}) by (job, instance))

panels.title: Status write failures by kind
panels.description: Objects per minute whose status update failed after conflict retries, by Kubernetes kind, on the replica that writes status. Typically RBAC (missing status update verbs for that kind) or an admission webhook rejecting the write. A write cut short because leadership ended is not counted.

targets.expr: sum by (kind) (rate(trickster_kgw_status_write_failures_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])) * 60

panels.title: Watch events by kind (busiest replica)
panels.description: Informer deliveries per second by watched Kubernetes kind, on the busiest replica (each replica runs its own informers, so the fleet sum would multiply this by the replica count). Expect an add spike at start-up and an update wave every resync_interval (10m by default) that changes nothing. Services, Secrets and ConfigMaps can dominate busy namespaces; watch_namespaces or namespace_selector narrows them. Top 10 kinds.

targets.expr: topk(10, max by (kind) (sum by (instance, kind) (rate(trickster_kgw_watch_events_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval]))))

panels.title: Watch events by type (busiest replica)
panels.description: Informer deliveries per second by event type, on the busiest replica. Every delivery marks the controller dirty and leads to a debounced reconcile pass. A steady stream of updates outside the resync waves means something in the cluster is rewriting watched objects continuously.

targets.expr: max by (event) (sum by (instance, event) (rate(trickster_kgw_watch_events_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Routing model by kind
panels.description: Size of the routing model the last compiled pass produced, by object class (largest replica). These are Trickster's generated objects, not Kubernetes objects: one HTTPRoute with several rules or backendRefs yields several routes and backends. A pass that fails to compile leaves the previous values; the series vanish briefly when a reload restarts the controller.

targets.expr: max by (kind) (trickster_kgw_generated_objects{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"})

panels.title: Replica divergence by kind
panels.description: Difference between the largest and smallest replica's routing-model count, per object class. 0 when every replica serves the same model; a short blip while a change propagates is normal, a lasting gap means a replica is failing its passes (see Reconcile passes by result).

targets.expr: max by (kind) (trickster_kgw_generated_objects{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}) - min by (kind) (trickster_kgw_generated_objects{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"})

panels.title: Routed objects by Kubernetes kind
panels.description: Kubernetes route objects the last compiled pass serves, by kind. TCPRoute, TLSRoute and UDPRoute need the experimental Gateway API CRDs. A route the controller refused (see its status conditions and Events) is not counted. The Backend filter applies.

targets.expr: count by (kind) (group by (kind, namespace, route) (group by (backend_name, kind, namespace, route) (label_replace(trickster_kgw_route_info{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}, "namespace", "$1", "exported_namespace", "(.+)"))))

panels.title: Route inventory
panels.description: Every generated backend in the last compiled model with the Kubernetes object it serves, and its HTTP request rate and 5xx share. A rule's route-facing backend ends in _r<rule>; when a rule has several backendRefs, that one is a load balancer and each ref gets a member backend ending in _b<ref> whose rows count the share sent to it again, so do not add member rows to the rule's row. TCPRoute, TLSRoute and UDPRoute backends carry stream traffic and always read 0 here. Click a backend to open it on the HTTP Traffic dashboard.

targets.expr: group by (backend_name, kind, namespace, route) (label_replace(trickster_kgw_route_info{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}, "namespace", "$1", "exported_namespace", "(.+)"))

(sum by (backend_name) (rate(trickster_frontend_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__rate_interval])) * on (backend_name) group_left (kind, namespace, route) group by (backend_name, kind, namespace, route) (label_replace(trickster_kgw_route_info{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}, "namespace", "$1", "exported_namespace", "(.+)"))) or (group by (backend_name, kind, namespace, route) (label_replace(trickster_kgw_route_info{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}, "namespace", "$1", "exported_namespace", "(.+)")) * 0)

(sum by (backend_name) (rate(trickster_frontend_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", http_status="5xx"}[$__rate_interval])) or sum by (backend_name) (rate(trickster_frontend_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__rate_interval])) * 0) / (sum by (backend_name) (rate(trickster_frontend_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0) * on (backend_name) group_left (kind, namespace, route) group by (backend_name, kind, namespace, route) (label_replace(trickster_kgw_route_info{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}, "namespace", "$1", "exported_namespace", "(.+)"))

value.title: Open this backend on HTTP Traffic

panels.title: Requests by route
panels.description: HTTP requests per second per Kubernetes route (Ingress, HTTPRoute, GRPCRoute), summed over its rules' route-facing backends only, so load-balancer member sub-requests are not counted twice. Includes requests the route answered itself (redirects, ACL or rate-limit refusals) and WebTransport CONNECTs for MoQ routes. Top 10 routes.

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (kind, namespace, route) (sum by (backend_name) (rate(trickster_frontend_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", backend_name=~".+_r[0-9]+"}[$__rate_interval])) * on (backend_name) group_left (kind, namespace, route) group by (backend_name, kind, namespace, route) (label_replace(trickster_kgw_route_info{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", backend_name=~".+_r[0-9]+"}, "namespace", "$1", "exported_namespace", "(.+)"))))

panels.title: 5xx share by route
panels.description: Share of each route's HTTP requests answered with a 5xx status, at its route-facing backends. A route with an unresolved backendRef answers its share of traffic with an error, so a steady 5xx share right after a change often means a ResolvedRefs problem on the route. Routes without any 5xx are not drawn. Top 10 routes.

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (kind, namespace, route) (sum by (backend_name) (rate(trickster_frontend_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", backend_name=~".+_r[0-9]+", http_status="5xx"}[$__rate_interval])) * on (backend_name) group_left (kind, namespace, route) group by (backend_name, kind, namespace, route) (label_replace(trickster_kgw_route_info{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", backend_name=~".+_r[0-9]+"}, "namespace", "$1", "exported_namespace", "(.+)"))) / (sum by (kind, namespace, route) (sum by (backend_name) (rate(trickster_frontend_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", backend_name=~".+_r[0-9]+"}[$__rate_interval])) * on (backend_name) group_left (kind, namespace, route) group by (backend_name, kind, namespace, route) (label_replace(trickster_kgw_route_info{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", backend_name=~".+_r[0-9]+"}, "namespace", "$1", "exported_namespace", "(.+)"))) > 0))

panels.title: Mean latency by route
panels.description: Average time to serve a request per Kubernetes route, at its route-facing backends, from request arrival to the end of the response. WebTransport CONNECTs (MoQ routes) are not timed. Means are used because the latency histogram's smallest bucket is 50 ms. Top 10 slowest routes.

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (kind, namespace, route) (sum by (backend_name) (rate(trickster_frontend_requests_duration_seconds_sum{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", backend_name=~".+_r[0-9]+"}[$__rate_interval])) * on (backend_name) group_left (kind, namespace, route) group by (backend_name, kind, namespace, route) (label_replace(trickster_kgw_route_info{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", backend_name=~".+_r[0-9]+"}, "namespace", "$1", "exported_namespace", "(.+)"))) / (sum by (kind, namespace, route) (sum by (backend_name) (rate(trickster_frontend_requests_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", backend_name=~".+_r[0-9]+"}[$__rate_interval])) * on (backend_name) group_left (kind, namespace, route) group by (backend_name, kind, namespace, route) (label_replace(trickster_kgw_route_info{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", backend_name=~".+_r[0-9]+"}, "namespace", "$1", "exported_namespace", "(.+)"))) > 0))
